d.d: A water-soluble organic compound, CO(NH₂)₂, formed by the metabolism of proteins and excreted in the urine.
Any N-substituted derivative of urea, with the general formula (R₁R₂N)CO(NR₃R₄).
Either of the two long, narrow ducts that carry urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.
A white crystalline organic compound, ethyl-carbamate, NH₂COOC₂H₅, used in the synthesis of other organic compounds.
Any compound consisting of this general structure.
